sections.h2: Which office takes a Wyandot County deed?
sections.html:
The Wyandot County Recorder works from Room 24 in the courthouse, 109 South Sandusky Avenue, Upper Sandusky, OH 43351, which also serves as the mailing address. Call 419-294-1442. Two deputy recorders work under the elected Recorder.

Wyandot is a rural county. Lawmakers carved it out on February 3, 1845 from Crawford, Marion, Hardin and Hancock counties. It spans 408 square miles of northwest Ohio and borders Seneca County to the north and Marion County to the south. Upper Sandusky is both the lone city and the seat. At the 2020 census Wyandot held 21,900 people, 9,084 households and 9,839 housing units, with vacancy at 7.7 percent. Owners occupy 73.5 percent of the occupied homes, and 69.7 percent of residents live outside urban areas.

That rural makeup shapes deeds here. Many Wyandot parcels are farm tracts or township acreage described by section, township and range, so the legal description gets more scrutiny than it would for a platted city lot.

sections.h2: Why does a deed stop at the Tax Map Department first?
sections.html:
The county's written conveyance standards say no deed will be accepted for transfer by the Auditor or for recording by the Recorder until the Engineer's Tax Map Department has reviewed and stamped it. The stamp reads Description Checked, Tax Map Office. The department has moved into the County Engineer's office at 320 N. Warpole Street.

The reviewer takes one of four paths on an ordinary sale with an unchanged description:

  • Approve the description as written and stamp the deed.
  • Suggest fixes for obvious typing errors, transposed numbers or rotated bearings, then stamp it.
  • Let a description with a clear point of beginning but minor flaws transfer one time, with a notice that a survey is required on the next non-exempt transfer.
  • Stamp a bad description Survey Required.

The standards define a bad description as one whose point of beginning cannot be identified or that contains an error causing ambiguity. Examples they list include missing dimensions or acreage, no section, township and range or municipality, and a parcel the grantor does not own. The standards invite deed writers to have a description checked ahead of closing, which leaves time for fixes.

sections.h2: Which Wyandot County transfers can skip a new survey?
sections.html:
An exempt transfer, with no money paid, can move on an older description that fails today's standards, and the deed gets the survey-required notice. The standards name survivorship, family trust moves, transfers to close family, life estates, corrective deeds, court-ordered transfers, and sheriff's and auditor's deeds.

A sale for money is a non-exempt transfer. If the house stands on an acreage tract with a vague description, plan on a survey request. New splits of an existing parcel need a survey recorded in the county survey records, a closure report, and at least three working days for inspection. New parcels need 40 feet of owned highway frontage for single family housing and 60 feet for multiple family housing. Parcels that miss the 200 foot road frontage rule in the regional planning checklist must meet those minimums. Call Wyandot County Regional Planning at 419-294-4931 before you plan a split.

sections.h2: What does a survey for a new Wyandot County lot have to show?
sections.html:
When an owner splits a house or acreage off a parent parcel, the survey checklist in the conveyance standards applies, and Wyandot Regional Planning in Room 16 of the courthouse reviews lots under its own rules. The checklist asks for these items:

  • A minimum property width of 200 feet and at least 1.50 acres, not counting highway right of way.
  • A lot length under four times its width.
  • Every structure, well and septic system drawn on the plat, with the distance to the nearest foot for any structure within 10 feet of a property line.
  • Required setbacks met.

Survey plats must be on quality bond or Mylar, at least 11 by 17 inches and in ink, so the Recorder can reproduce and microfilm them. When a parent parcel is divided into five or more smaller parcels, the splits are reviewed under major subdivision requirements, and earlier splits from the same parent count toward the five.

sections.h2: What do the Ohio statutes require of the deed itself?
sections.html:
Under Revised Code 5301.01 the grantor signs and has the signature acknowledged by an authorized officer, usually a notary. Revised Code 317.13 has the Recorder log each instrument with its date and the minute it arrived, so filing order settles priority.

The same section lets a recorder turn down a paper that the Code does not authorize or that looks fraudulent, with a court remedy for the filer. It also set a June 30, 2026 deadline for electronic recording and online indexes reaching back to 1980. Ask the Wyandot office which electronic options it offers.

sections.h2: Which transfers owe the Auditor's conveyance fee?
sections.html:
Most sales do, and the seller pays. Revised Code 319.54 states the fee as one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars, whichever is greater, and Revised Code 319.202 has the buyer file a statement of value first. In a sale, value is the whole consideration, with any mortgage on the property counted in.

Transfers the statute excludes from the Auditor's conveyance fee
Type of transferFee under 319.54(G)(3)
Gift between spouses, or parent and childNot charged
Among heirs or devisees of one decedent, no money paidNot charged
Into a trust the grantor can revokeNot charged
To confirm or correct a recorded deedNot charged
Sale to a buyer for moneyCharged at the rate above

Source: Ohio Revised Code 319.54. The statute lists more exemptions, such as court ordered transfers that are not sales.

Revised Code 322.02 also lets a county adopt its own transfer tax. Ask the Wyandot County Auditor whether one applies.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Wyandot County Recorder?
sections.html:
The page-based charges in Revised Code 317.32 are the same statewide, and the Recorder can quote your total. A long metes and bounds description adds pages, so ask before you mail the deed.

Pull the previous deed before the new one is typed. The standards require any new metes and bounds description to cite the prior deed and the source of each exception, and the acreage must be shown to three decimal places. A tract may carry no more than four exceptions.

sections.h2: How do I research a Wyandot County parcel before listing it?
sections.html:
The Tax Map Department also helps the public find property, check ownership and obtain new addresses in unincorporated areas. Its county page offers downloads of tax maps, property surveys and legal descriptions, plus a current parcel data file in ZIP format that the county supplies as is, with no guarantee of accuracy. The County Auditor keeps an online tax map site as well.

The county describes this as a tax map system rather than a full GIS and has no GIS department for advanced requests. An owner with an older farm or edge-of-town house can collect three items early:

  • The parcel number and acreage the Auditor shows on the tax map.
  • The last recorded deed, with its legal description and any exceptions.
  • Any recorded survey for the tract, which settles whether a survey will be demanded on the next transfer.

Comparing the deed acreage with the tax map matters because the standards for older descriptions that are not metes and bounds tolerate a difference of only 0.2 acre on parcels under 5 acres and 5 percent on larger ones.

faqs.q: Is a survey required for a Wyandot County house?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A sale with an unchanged description moves after the Tax Map stamp. A bad description earns a Survey Required stamp, and any split of a parcel needs a recorded survey.

faqs.q: Where is the Wyandot County Tax Map Department?
faqs.a: It operates from the County Engineer's office at 320 N. Warpole Street in Upper Sandusky, after moving from its earlier location.

faqs.q: Who covers the Auditor's fee in Wyandot County?
faqs.a: The seller. The statute measures it at the greater of one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars of value.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Wyandot County Recorder?
faqs.a: Phone 419-294-1442, or visit Room 24 of the courthouse at 109 South Sandusky Avenue.

faqs.q: Can a deed be turned away?
faqs.a: Yes, if the paper is not authorized for recording or looks fraudulent. The filer can go to court to seek an order.
